lesson: Unlock your English: phrases that work today (A1 · Aula 0)

cards.definition: Used to say what your opinion is.
cards.example:
- I think we need one more week for this project.
Acho que precisamos de mais uma semana para este projeto.
- I don't think so, but I can check.
Acho que não, mas posso verificar.
- I think she is right about the price.
Acho que ela está certa sobre o preço.
cards.note: Abre qualquer opinião sem soar arrogante. O negativo vem no think: I don't think it works, e não I think it doesn't work. Resposta curta pronta: I don't think so.

cards.definition: Used to say that you must have something.
cards.example:
- I need more information before I answer the client.
Preciso de mais informação antes de responder ao cliente.
- I need to leave at five today.
Preciso sair às cinco hoje.
- I need your help with this email.
Preciso da sua ajuda com este e-mail.
cards.note: Não use of depois de need: I need help, I need time. Antes de um verbo entra to: I need to talk to you. O passado é I needed.

cards.definition: A polite way to say what you want.
cards.example:
- I'd like a coffee, please — and I'd like to ask something.
Eu queria um café, por favor — e queria perguntar uma coisa.
- I'd like to start the meeting now.
Eu gostaria de começar a reunião agora.
- I'd like a window seat, please.
Eu queria um lugar na janela, por favor.
cards.note: É a forma curta de I would like e soa bem mais educado que I want. Antes de verbo vem to: I'd like to ask. Antes de substantivo, nada: I'd like a coffee.

cards.definition: A short and polite way to ask for permission.
cards.example:
- Can I ask a question about the deadline?
Posso fazer uma pergunta sobre o prazo?
- Can I call you back in ten minutes?
Posso te ligar de volta em dez minutos?
- Can I use your pen for a second?
Posso usar sua caneta por um segundo?
cards.note: Pedido rápido e educado; em situação formal, May I…? soa ainda mais polido. Depois de Can I vem o verbo sem to: Can I ask a question? Para pedir que o outro faça algo, use Can you…?

cards.definition: The question you use to ask for a word in English.
cards.example:
- How do you say “prazo” in English?
Como se diz “prazo” em inglês?
- How do you say that in a formal email?
Como se diz isso num e-mail formal?
- I forgot the word — how do you say it?
Esqueci a palavra — como se diz isso?
cards.note: É a pergunta que mantém a conversa em inglês em vez de travar. Termine com in English: How do you say this in English? Para pronúncia, a pergunta é How do you pronounce this?

cards.definition: The question you use to ask for the meaning of a word.
cards.example:
- What does “ASAP” mean, exactly?
O que significa “ASAP”, exatamente?
- What does this word mean?
O que significa esta palavra?
- What does “on hold” mean in a call?
O que significa “on hold” numa ligação?
cards.note: Nunca finja que entendeu: perguntar soa profissional, não fraco. A palavra fica no meio: What does “deadline” mean? No plural, use What do these words mean?

cards.definition: A phrase you use before an answer you are not certain about.
cards.example:
- I'm not sure, but I think the meeting is on Friday.
Não tenho certeza, mas acho que a reunião é sexta.
- I'm not sure, but I can check with my manager.
Não tenho certeza, mas posso verificar com meu gerente.
- I'm not sure, but the file went out yesterday.
Não tenho certeza, mas o arquivo saiu ontem.
cards.note: Permite participar sem medo de errar e soa honesto, não inseguro. Depois dela vem uma frase completa: I'm not sure, but I think so. Para dizer só “não sei”, use I don't know.

cards.definition: A polite way to ask someone to say something again.
cards.example:
- Sorry, could you repeat that, please? A little slower.
Desculpe, pode repetir, por favor? Um pouco mais devagar.
- Could you repeat that, please? The line is bad.
Pode repetir, por favor? A ligação está ruim.
- I didn't catch the address. Could you repeat that, please?
Não peguei o endereço. Pode repetir, por favor?
cards.note: Peça sem se desculpar demais e combine com a little slower quando precisar. Could soa mais educado que can. Outra saída pronta: Sorry, I didn't catch that.

cards.definition: Used to say what is really true, often to correct something.
cards.example:
- Actually, I like online meetings — they save me two hours.
Na verdade, eu gosto de reuniões online — economizam duas horas.
- Actually, my name is Ana, not Ana Maria.
Na verdade, meu nome é Ana, não Ana Maria.
- It looks hard, but it is actually easy.
Parece difícil, mas na verdade é fácil.
cards.note: “Atualmente” é currently; actually corrige uma impressão errada. No começo da frase vem com vírgula: Actually, I sent it. Cuidado com o tom ao corrigir alguém.

cards.definition: To act as if something is true when it is not.
cards.example:
- He pretends to understand everything in the call.
Ele finge que entende tudo na reunião.
- I pretended to be busy when he called.
Fingi estar ocupado quando ele ligou.
- Children love to pretend they are pilots.
Crianças adoram fingir que são pilotos.
cards.note: “Pretendo estudar mais” não é I pretend: é I intend to ou I plan to. Passado: pretended. Depois vem to + verbo (pretend to know) ou that (pretend that you know).

exercise.title: Unlock your English: phrases that work today (A1 · Aula 0)

questions.prompt: You want permission to leave ten minutes early. What do you ask?
options: Can I leave ten minutes early?
Can you leave ten minutes early?
Do I leave ten minutes early?
I can leave ten minutes early.
questions.answer: Can I leave ten minutes early?
questions.explanation: “Can I…?” asks for permission for yourself.

questions.prompt: Before the call, _____ five minutes to check the numbers.
questions.explanation: “I need” says that something is necessary for you.

questions.prompt: Acho que segunda-feira é melhor para todo mundo.
questions.answer: I think Monday is better for everyone.|I think that Monday is better for everyone.

questions.prompt: You do not know a word in English. What do you ask your teacher?
options: What does this mean in English?
How do you say this in English?
How do you spell this in English?
Can you repeat this in English?
questions.answer: How do you say this in English?
questions.explanation: “How do you say…?” asks for a word you do not know yet.

questions.prompt: Eu gostaria de falar com o gerente.
questions.answer: I'd like to speak to the manager.|I'd like to talk to the manager.
questions.explanation: “I'd like” is the polite way to say what you want.

questions.prompt: The report is not late; it is _____ ready.
A colleague writes “EOD” and you do not know the word. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: “What does … mean?” asks for the meaning of a word.

questions.prompt: Please don't _____ to understand — just ask me to repeat.
questions.explanation: To “pretend” is to act as if something is true when it is not.

questions.prompt: Não ouvi o número. Pode repetir, por favor?
questions.answer: I didn't hear the number. Could you repeat that, please?|Sorry, I didn't hear the number. Could you repeat that, please?
questions.explanation: “Could you repeat that, please?” asks someone to say it again.

questions.prompt: You think the answer is Friday, but you are not certain. How do you start?
questions.explanation: “I'm not sure, but…” lets you answer without promising it is right.
